meaning: Q-MORAL-ERROR, emotivist cell. Moral error is a false belief: accepting a sentence that has a truth value and is not true (TruthCore.Metaethics.Errs, the notion the question uses; Aquinas, ST I-II q.94 a.6, likens moral to speculative error). O'Connor's emotivism denies every moral sentence a truth value, so no one errs about a moral matter, the consequence Carnap drew (SEP §2.2, claim SEP-MORAL-COGNITIVISM-2-2-CARNAP-NO-MORAL-ERROR). Proof shape, stated plainly: two steps through the definition of error; the premise does not state the conclusion. Scope: the result reaches only the denial of truth value 'at all'. Quasi-realism's minimal truth escapes it (QUASI-REALISM-ADMITS-MORAL-ERROR). It shows what emotivism must say, not that emotivism is false. Against Aquinas's datum (AQUINAS-ST-I-II-Q94-A4-GERMANS-ERRED) it is recorded as an attack, since that datum is itself an open premise.
